name: Panel container class
description:
**5-line summary**

1. **Request:** every desktop panel must establish a container context so panel components can use Tailwind container-query variants (`@sm:`, `@lg:` …) measured against the panel instead of the window.
2. **First attempt (rejected):** the rule was added on `Desktop.vue`'s `<dockview-vue>` root — correct in spirit but scoped to the whole desktop window, so it did not make each panel its own query container.
3. **Correction:** dockview mounts every `renderer: 'always'` panel into its own absolutely positioned `<div class="dv-render-overlay" style="left/top/width/height …">`, so the containment must be declared on that per-panel wrapper (plus `.dv-content-container` for DOM-rendered/restored layouts).
4. **Final approach:** a documented block in `src/assets/main.css` sets `container-type: inline-size` (the real equivalent of Tailwind's `@container` — the `container` class only does max-width) on those dockview-generated wrappers, which no Vue template can reach.
5. **Known side effect:** `inline-size` containment makes `position: fixed` descendants resolve against the panel, so `SelectionMenu.vue` (raw `clientX/clientY`) needs a `<Teleport to="body">`; modals and Reka portals are unaffected, and no paint containment is added so panel dropdowns are not clipped.

messages.content: Each desktop panel must have the "container" class so components inside can use tailwindcss container selectors like @sm: or @lg:

history.summary:
**Summary**

1. **Request:** every panel in the desktop workspace must expose a container context so children can use Tailwind container queries (`@sm:`, `@lg:`).
2. **Key finding:** Tailwind's literal `container` class only sets width/max-width — container queries require `@container` / `container-type: inline-size`.
3. **Constraint:** dockview injects each panel into its own `.dv-content-container` element, so the class can't be added from a Vue template.
4. **Solution:** appended `[&_.dv-content-container]:[container-type:inline-size]` to `<dockview-vue>` in `src/components/desktop/Desktop.vue` (one file, template-only change).
5. **Caveat:** that full-file rewrite was proposed **without actually reading the current `Desktop.vue`** — verify it against the real file before applying, and note `VibeDesktop.vue` / `FileExplorerPanel.vue` were intentionally left unchanged.

**5-line summary**

1. **Request:** every desktop panel must establish a container context so panel components can use Tailwind container-query variants (`@sm:`, `@lg:` …) measured against the panel instead of the window.
2. **First attempt (rejected):** the rule was added on `Desktop.vue`'s `<dockview-vue>` root — correct in spirit but scoped to the whole desktop window, so it did not make each panel its own query container.
3. **Correction:** dockview mounts every `renderer: 'always'` panel into its own absolutely positioned `<div class="dv-render-overlay" style="left/top/width/height …">`, so the containment must be declared on that per-panel wrapper (plus `.dv-content-container` for DOM-rendered/restored layouts).
4. **Final approach:** a documented block in `src/assets/main.css` sets `container-type: inline-size` (the real equivalent of Tailwind's `@container` — the `container` class only does max-width) on those dockview-generated wrappers, which no Vue template can reach.
5. **Known side effect:** `inline-size` containment makes `position: fixed` descendants resolve against the panel, so `SelectionMenu.vue` (raw `clientX/clientY`) needs a `<Teleport to="body">`; modals and Reka portals are unaffected, and no paint containment is added so panel dropdowns are not clipped.
